validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification/duplicate. Real, correctly classified transmission trunk, and NOT a duplicate of P0789 (Urengoy-Novopskov) or P0791 (Orenburg-Novopskov) despite the very similar names/hub — name the distinction explicitly in ResearcherNotes if a future cluster-adjudication pass revisits the Novopskov family, so it isn't re-litigated.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: eegas.com (Mike Fulwood's specialist Ukraine-gas-transit analysis site, cited by the sheet's own wiki page) lists 'Petrovsk-Novopskov (Pisarevka): 14 bcm/yr, 1 line' in its table of Ukraine's major import pipelines from Russia — an exact match to GEM's Capacity=14.00 bcm/y, from a named entry point (Pisarevka) that lines up with GEM's own EndLocation family. Independently, energyland.info (industry trade press, dated 2026-06-29) reports Gazprom Transgaz Volgograd completing scheduled repair works on the 'main gas pipeline Petrovsk-Novopskov,' naming three of its own linear-production-management (LPUMG) stations — Bubnovsky, Kalacheevsky, Pisarevsky, all in Voronezh Oblast, geographically between Petrovsk (Saratov Oblast) and the Ukrainian border at Pisarevka — as of mid-2026, i.e. very recent, active, in-service maintenance on this exact named asset. Two independent sources, 17 years apart, both describing the same physical pipe as functioning. A straight-line distance check (Petrovsk, Saratov Oblast ~52.31N 45.39E, to Novopskov, Luhansk Oblast ~49.53N 39.11E) gives ~538 km great-circle vs. the sheet's 609 km routed length — a plausible ~13% routing overhead for a real cross-country trunk, not evidence of a phantom or wildly-off figure. DUPLICATE CHECK: I actively checked this against the roster because P0790 (Petrovsk->Novopskov, 609 km, 1220mm, 14.0 bcm/y), P0789 (Urengoy-Novopskov, 3609 km, 1400mm, 31.0 bcm/y) and P0791 (Orenburg-Novopskov, 1230 km, 1220mm, 14.6 bcm/y) all converge on the same Novopskov hub with two of the three sharing the 1220mm diameter class. eegas.com's own table resolves this cleanly: it lists Urengoy-Novopskov (Pisarevka, 31 bcm/yr), Petrovsk-Novopskov (Pisarevka, 14 bcm/yr) and Orenburg-Novopskov (Sokhranovka, 18 bcm/yr) as THREE SEPARATE line items with three different capacities and, notably, two different physical border-crossing points (Pisarevka vs. Sokhranovka) — i.e. an independent specialist source treating them as distinct pipes, not a segment breakdown of one line. (Separately, eegas.com's 18 bcm/yr for Orenburg-Novopskov vs. the sheet's 14.6 for P0791 is a discrepancy worth a look on THAT row, but it's out of scope here and doesn't bear on P0790's own numbers.) I also found Russian-language procurement/engineering documents describing reconstruction of 'Urengoy-Novopskov газопровод на участке Петровск-Писаревка' (Urengoy-Novopskov pipeline at the Petrovsk-Pisarevka section) — this describes MULTIPLE Soviet-era trunks bundled through the same physical corridor/right-of-way between Petrovsk and Pisarevka for a shared reconstruction project (ahead of South Stream feed-in), not evidence that Petrovsk-Novopskov IS Urengoy-Novopskov under another name. Given the independent eegas.com table entry with its own distinct capacity and border point, I'm treating P0790 as a genuinely separate physical pipe from both P0789 and P0791.

eegas.com's pipeline name itself ('Petrovsk-Novopskov (Pisarevka)') confirms both endpoints and the specific border-crossing point (Pisarevka, on the Voronezh Oblast/Ukraine border) consistent with GEM's Petrovsk(Saratov Oblast, Russia)->Novopskov(Luhansk, Ukraine) routing. energyland.info independently confirms the route passes through Bubnovsky and Kalacheevsky LPUMG stations (Voronezh Oblast, between Saratov and the border) then Pisarevsky LPUMG (at the border) — geographically consistent with a Petrovsk-to-Novopskov route via Voronezh Oblast.
